simple-google-analytics-alternative:
Google Analytics 4 is free and very capable. It is also built for marketing teams that live inside Google Ads, build custom reports and model attribution across devices. If you run a docs site, a SaaS landing page or a side project, you probably want answers to a much shorter list of questions.

What most small sites actually need

  • Traffic: page views, unique visitors and sessions over time.
  • Sources: which referrers and UTM campaigns send visitors.
  • Content: top pages, entry pages and exit pages.
  • Actions: a handful of custom events, such as signup_completed or docs_copied.
  • A dashboard you can read in a minute, without building reports first.

If that list covers you, a simpler tool is usually a better fit than GA4.

What you give up compared with GA4

Being honest about trade-offs matters more than feature checklists:

  • Google Ads integration. GA4 connects to Google Ads, Search Ads 360, Display & Video 360 and Search Console. If you buy Google ads and optimise on conversions, that integration is hard to replace.
  • Cross-device user modelling. GA4 uses first-party cookies (_ga, with a default two-year expiry) to distinguish returning users, according to Google's own documentation (as of Oct 2026). Pulzivo sets no cookies and collects no personal data, so it does not try to follow one person across devices.
  • Price. GA4's standard tier is free of charge (as of Oct 2026). Pulzivo also has a free plan, but higher volumes are paid.

What you get with a simpler tool

  • Setup in one step. Add a script tag and page views are tracked automatically. Paid plans add automatic click and scroll tracking, sessions, unique visitors and UTM attribution (see pricing for what each plan includes).
  • No cookies, no personal data. Pulzivo does not set cookies and does not collect personal data from your visitors.
  • A small script. The Pulzivo tracker is about 9KB gzipped.
  • Custom events with one call, from plain HTML or any framework.

Setting up Pulzivo

Create an account, copy your API key from the dashboard, and add the script to your site's <head>:

<script src="https://cdn.pulzivo.com/pulzivo-analytics.min.js"
        data-api-key="YOUR_API_KEY"></script>

Then track the actions you care about:

PulzivoAnalytics('event', 'signup_completed', { plan: 'free' });

It works the same in React, Vue, Angular, Next.js, Svelte or plain HTML because the SDK exposes a global function. See the documentation for configuration options.

Running both side by side

You do not have to switch in one go. Add Pulzivo next to GA4 for a few weeks, check that the numbers tell the same story for your top pages and sources, then decide whether you still need GA4. Expect counts to differ somewhat between any two tools because of ad blockers, bot filtering and different definitions of a session.

privacy-friendly-analytics-small-sites:
"Privacy-friendly analytics" is used loosely. This checklist is a practical way to decide what to measure on a small site and how to evaluate a tool, including Pulzivo. It is not legal advice: whether you need consent or a banner depends on your jurisdiction and everything else on your site, so check with someone qualified.

1. Decide what questions you need answered

Write down the three to five questions you actually look at. For most small sites they are: how many people visit, where they come from, which pages they read, and whether they complete the one or two actions that matter (signup, download, contact). Anything you will not look at is data you do not need to collect.

2. Prefer aggregate data over individual profiles

Counts per page, per referrer and per country answer the questions above without building a profile of any individual visitor. Pulzivo is designed around this: no cookies, no personal data.

3. Check how the tool identifies visits

Ask the vendor directly: does the script set cookies? Does it store anything on the device? Does it collect IP addresses, and if so, are they stored? For comparison, Google's documentation states that GA4's JavaScript tags use first-party cookies such as _ga (two-year default expiry) to distinguish users (as of Oct 2026). Pulzivo sets no cookies and collects no personal data.

4. Keep custom events free of personal data

The tool is only half the story. If you send an email address or a name as an event property, you have put personal data into your analytics regardless of which vendor you use. Use IDs that mean nothing outside your system, or none at all:

// Good
PulzivoAnalytics('event', 'signup_completed', { plan: 'starter' });

// Avoid
PulzivoAnalytics('event', 'signup_completed', { email: user.email });

5. Look at data retention

Keep data only as long as you use it. On Pulzivo, retention depends on the plan: 30 days on Free, 6 months on Starter, 12 months on Pro and 24 months on Enterprise (see pricing).

6. Weigh script size, but do not obsess

A smaller analytics script is good for page speed, but most of your page weight is usually images, fonts and your own JavaScript. Pulzivo's tracker is about 9KB gzipped. Measure your own pages before and after adding any tool.

7. Update your privacy policy

Whatever tool you choose, describe what you collect and why in plain language on your privacy page.

pulzivo-vs-ga4-vs-plausible-pricing:
Analytics pricing pages are hard to compare because vendors meter different things. This page lists what each vendor published on its own site when we checked in October 2026. Prices change, so follow the links before you decide.

What is being counted

  • Pulzivo meters events per month (page views, clicks and custom events all count).
  • Plausible and Fathom meter monthly pageviews. Fathom states that custom events count towards the same allowance.
  • GA4 standard is free of charge.

Because Pulzivo counts clicks and custom events as well as page views, the same traffic can use more Pulzivo events than it would use pageviews elsewhere. Run Pulzivo on the free plan for a few weeks to see your real monthly event count before picking a tier.

Google Analytics 4

Google describes Google Analytics as giving you the tools "free of charge" (Google Marketing Platform, as of Oct 2026). The cost is not money: GA4 uses first-party cookies such as _ga to distinguish users (Google Analytics Help, as of Oct 2026), and it takes more time to set up and learn.

Plausible

At the 10k monthly pageviews tier, Plausible lists Starter at $9/month, Growth at $14/month and Business at $19/month (plausible.io, as of Oct 2026). Higher pageview tiers cost more; use their slider for exact figures.

Fathom

Fathom's plans start at $15/month for up to 100,000 monthly pageviews, with 50 sites included and a 7-day free trial that requires a card. Fathom states it does not offer a free plan (usefathom.com/pricing, as of Oct 2026).

How to choose

  • You rely on Google Ads conversion data: GA4 is hard to replace.
  • You want a free plan without cookies or personal data, plus custom events: start with Pulzivo Free.
  • You have many small sites: check how many sites each plan includes, not just the traffic limit.
  • You are not sure about volume: run the tool alongside your current analytics for a few weeks before committing.
